rule: The words, trimmed, go into the composer: words empty after trimming leave it as it is; a composer empty after trimming becomes the words; a composer that already holds the words verbatim (a UTF-16 match: JS indexOf, NSString range(of:options:.literal)) is left as it is; any other composer becomes the words, a line feed, then the composer as it was.
notes: composer: the box the words go into (the web composer for screens.off {screen:'coach', draft}; the native one for CoachStore's putBack and a page draft). words: the words handed in. result: the composer after.

Trimming is JS String.prototype.trim() and Swift's .whitespacesAndNewlines. They differ on three characters, checked over every code point (macOS 27 Foundation, Node 25): U+FEFF (JS trims it, Swift does not), U+0085 and U+200B (Swift trims them, JS does not). No case uses them.
Every string is well-formed UTF-16 (no lone surrogate).
Read by CoachStoreTests (CoachStore.mergeDraft) and by the page's specs (the screens.off handler). A rule change edits this file first.
